convention_compliance.workflow_naming: deviation: 'license_grant_workflow', 'license_revocation_workflow', and 'license_suspension_workflow' use the <Action>Workflow snake_case form rather than the recommended <Verb>By<Role> pattern (e.g., 'license_granted_by_regulator'). Recommended fix: rename to '<verb>_by_<role>' form on next minor version.

author_intent_notes:
Worked example produced via the micro-app-template-gen skill on 2026-05-11; migrated to CEL/1.0 on 2026-07-13 (Stage 3 of the expression-language migration, docs/superpowers/plans/2026-07-13-uel-cel-migration.md). Authoring scenario: state Department of Insurance receives carrier license applications, adjudicates them, issues carrier_license credentials, and manages their full lifecycle (suspension, reinstatement, revocation). Complements the existing carrier-applies-for-license worked example as the regulator's side of the bilateral conversation. Together, the two micro-apps demonstrate the decentralized authoring pattern: each side is independently authored from its own role's perspective; composition emerges at runtime via KERI-native IPEX exchange (apply -> grant or spurn -> admit or spurn).

Unlike the carrier-side example, this template exercises the full credential-export envelope: a real JSON-Schema file in schemas/, a four-state lifecycle (pending -> active -> suspended -> revoked) with all three TEL primitives (issue, update, revoke), and rule_refs binding the lifecycle to predicates (financial_solvency_demonstrated for activate, suspension_grounds_cleared for reinstate). The credentials.imports list is intentionally empty: the regulator's authority is KEL-anchored regulatory power, not a held credential.

CEL/1.0 expressions are written against the bound-context cheat-sheet (references/cel-1.0-cheat-sheet.md). As part of the 2026-07-13 migration every expression in this template was compile-checked against cel-python 0.5.0 (the pinned CEL/1.0 runtime evaluator), and every test_vectors entry was executed through a reference fold engine implementing the accepted spec's reference semantics (docs/superpowers/specs/2026-07-10-cel-declarative-aggregates-and-projections.md §11) — all vectors reproduce their declared expected state. Notable expression decisions:
  - state_preconditions on grant_license / spurn_application use the .exists(x, ...) comma-macro pattern over state.pending_applications, per the cheat-sheet idiom for 'does this aggregate row exist?'.
  - financial_solvency_demonstrated and suspension_grounds_cleared bind to lifecycle_transition_requires context, whose bindings include credential.attributes (cheat-sheet §2). The expressions reference market_conduct_status as a proxy for the underlying determination; the regulator's signature on the grant_license command is the operational gate.
  - applicant_provided_all_required_fields uses notNull() (cheat-sheet §5 extension function) for presence checks and size(...) (not the old .length property) on lines_of_business.
  - no_duplicate_active_license_per_carrier uses the canonical 'at most one per group' invariant pattern from cheat-sheet §6, rewritten from the earlier arrow-lambda .every/.filter/.length idiom to CEL's .all(x, ...)/.filter(x, ...)/size(...).
  - The aggregate now carries an explicit fold handler map (template spec §6.5), replacing the earlier implicit reaction-driven fold: application_received/application_withdrawn/application_denied/license_granted are op-list handlers; license_suspended/license_reinstated/license_revoked are raw reducers because moving a license between active_licenses/suspended_licenses/revoked_licenses while enriching it with the transition's own fields (suspension_reason, revocation_reason, etc.) is beyond what the op vocabulary's single-field ops (append/remove/move) can express in one step. boundary.instance_key is a constant ('license_registry') because this aggregate is a single per-deployment registry (one instance per regulator), not partitioned by any event field.
  - Migrating the fold surfaced a latent state_schema gap: suspended_licenses and revoked_licenses previously carried only their own transition fields (e.g. suspension_reason/suspended_at) and dropped jurisdiction/lines_of_business/effective_date/expiration_date/granted_at, so reinstating a suspended license could never restore a complete active_licenses row. Fixed by adding those fields to both arrays' item schemas (required) so a license's full record survives suspend -> reinstate and suspend/active -> revoke round trips: retaining the data is the only behavior under which the aggregate's own reinstate transition is expressible at all, so this is a data-completeness correction, not a design fork.
  - pending_applications and active_licenses_in_state projections are migrated to shape: "collection" with primary_key (application_id / license_said respectively), an explicit fold handler map (upsert on receipt/grant, delete on the events that used to filter the row out), and ordering: "source_seq" (single log). output_schema is renamed row_schema per the amended template spec.
  - All map literals in every expression use quoted string keys ({ "application_id": command.application_id }, never { application_id: ... }): CEL map-literal keys are expressions, so a bare identifier key evaluates as an unbound variable — verified failure on cel-python 0.5.0.
  - All payload_mapping expressions follow the per-trigger bindings: reactions on exn_received use event.<field> (event envelope flattened with the payload; no .payload. nesting), command emissions use command.<field>. NOTE: grant_license's license_granted payload_mapping does not currently populate license_said or holder_aid on the emitted event (pre-existing gap, not introduced by this migration) even though the new aggregate/projection fold handlers for license_granted read event.license_said/event.holder_aid; this migration mechanically ports the old fold_expression's own assumption about those fields rather than redesigning the emitting side, since Stage 4 (wiring cel-python into command compute) is where payload_mapping correctness against real command output gets addressed end-to-end. Flagged as an open risk below.
  - idempotency_key_expression is gone (removed from the template spec during canon consolidation per THE DECISION §3.6 amendment 4; the runtime dedups on the exn SAID instead) — this template never carried one.

Adversarial review performed 2026-05-11; re-reviewed 2026-07-13 for the CEL/1.0 migration. Walked checklist items 1-10. Identified concerns:
  1. Impersonation: grant_license has no auth_preconditions referencing a held regulator-authority credential because the regulator's KEL is the root authority for licensing in its jurisdiction (the spec's recommended pattern for government roles). Acceptable for v1.0; a delegated-authority refinement would add an auth_precondition gating on a regulator_authority credential when the DOI delegates licensing to a contracted reviewer.
  2. Credential revocation timing: revoke_license fires lifecycle_advance to revoked and a TEL revocation event. Holders observe via their watcher network; the carrier-side template's on_license_revoked reaction folds this. Race between revoke and renewal is undefined and worth surfacing in a future revision.
  3. Concurrent commands: two grant_license commands on the same application_id are both gated by application_pending_for_grant; the winner advances the application out of pending, the loser fails on stale state. UI behavior on the losing command is undefined.
  4. Missed events: pending_applications and active_licenses_in_state projections now fold via explicit upsert/delete handlers (idempotent by construction — upsert-by-primary_key, delete-by-routed-row) rather than the earlier implicit filter/concat description.
  5. Counterparty bad behavior: step_await_admit in license_grant_workflow has time_bound P30D; if the carrier never admits the grant, step_grant_lapsed terminates the workflow. No reissuance path is modeled in v1.0 (would require an admit-or-reissue branch).
  6. Compromised actor keys: KERI rotation semantics apply to both the regulator's signing key (recovery via pre-rotation) and the carrier's holder key. Aggregate respects key state at command time. Acceptable.
  7. Schema versioning: the carrier_license schema's SAID is content-addressed (ELK09oTcRiiv-Zmxl-rjKo6EVyOLV-5o4SK96g1kSUie). A v2 schema would have a new SAID; the regulator would issue under a new exported_credential. Projection fold handlers are schema-version-agnostic because they read the folded event's typed payload fields, not the credential's schema.
  8. Convention divergence: workflow naming deviation noted above.
  9. Idempotency under network retry: this template has no idempotency_key_expression (field removed from the spec); the runtime dedups on the exn message's SAID instead.
  10. Permission escalation via chained credentials: not applicable — no edges in the envelope (the regulator's authority is root, not derived).

Open risks: (a) grant_license's license_granted payload_mapping does not yet populate license_said/holder_aid — the aggregate and active_licenses_in_state fold handlers for license_granted assume those fields exist on the folded event; this needs to be resolved when Stage 4 wires cel-python into command compute (either enrich the payload_mapping, e.g. by reading the pending application's applicant_aid from state and minting/reading the credential's own SAID, or adjust the fold to source them elsewhere). (b) license_reinstated is a no-op in the active_licenses_in_state projection (mirrors the pre-migration fold_expression's own behavior): a reinstated license does not reappear in that projection's rows, only in the aggregate's active_licenses array, because the projection's fold context ({row, event}) cannot recover the row's other fields once license_suspended has already deleted it; worth a future revision once the emitting events carry richer payloads. (c) The financial_solvency_demonstrated and suspension_grounds_cleared expressions are operationally gated by the regulator's manual approval; the formal predicate is a placeholder for a richer assessment in future versions. (d) The regulator-authority delegation refinement noted in adversarial-review item 1 remains open, unaffected by this migration.
